subject: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - Nimbus Analytics (Hosted → Dedicated cutover plan)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - initial ask

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass capacity proposal that maps Nimbus's current Hosted API usage to a Dedicated GPU fleet. The goals here are to:

- Validate that the proposed GPU counts meet both steady-state QPS and peak burst targets
- Confirm expected cost delta and identify quick wins (batching, KV caching, quantization)
- Outline a pragmatic cutover timeline and a 30‑day dry-run for traffic validation

If you can share the 90-day aggregate and 7‑day peak metrics we can tighten the sizing (a CSV would be perfect). I cc'd Marissa and Dev to run a quick sizing calc and flag any redlines for procurement.

Attached: capacity-proposal-nimbus-v1.pdf

Proposed action items:
1) Sam: send 7-day peak RPS + p50/p95 latency numbers (or the CSV you mentioned) — by Tue 3/3
2) Redwood: Marissa/Dev will produce a BOM and initial GPU count by Wed 3/4
3) Align on a 2‑week cutover window and a 30‑day dry-run after Dedicated is provisioned

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Lee <sam@NimbusAnalytics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:23:45 -0500
Subject: Re: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - initial ask

Thanks Aisha — attaching the 7‑day peak export and a 90‑day summary. High level before you dig in:

- Steady state: ~350 concurrent generator calls/min (p50 latency ~180ms hosted)
- Peak short bursts: ~2.1k concurrent over 2–3 minute windows (p95 spikes to ~750ms)
- Token mix: 60% short prompts (~100 tokens), 40% longer context (~1.6k tokens)
- We use streaming heavily for UX flows; KV cache is not currently used in Hosted setup

We are sensitive to cost but cannot accept >15% regression in p95 compared to hosted. Procurement copied for visibility — they will want a BOM and lead time for any GPU procurements.

Attached: nimbus-current-traffic-2026-02.csv

- Sam
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:40:12 -0800
Subject: RE: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - initial ask

Aisha / team —

I ran a quick mapping from Nimbus's CSV to Redwood's fleet assumptions. Key callouts below — this is an initial validation, not final procurement numbers.

Sizing summary (initial):
- Baseline: 4x A100‑80GB-equivalent nodes (mixed precision, 16‑bit) to handle steady state with continuous batching; autoscale pool + 2 spare nodes for failover
- Peak handling: scale to 12 nodes for sustained 3‑minute bursts (based on observed 2.1k concurrent)
- For your token mix, enabling KV caching for the 40% long-context flows reduces repeated prefix compute by ~35% in our sim
- Quantization option (Q4) could reduce nodes by ~20% at minor p95 cost increase; we should validate quality with your eval prompts

Estimated lead times and procurement:
- If using Hosted Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity): 2–3 weeks to provision GPU pool once commit is approved
- Private on-prem procurement adds 6–10 weeks (hardware lead times)

Notes:
- I attached a BOM with per-node cost + SKU assumptions (redwood-bom-gpu-estimates.xlsx).
- We should run a 30‑day dry-run on Dedicated with traffic mirroring before cutover to ensure p95 parity.

Action items for this thread:
- Priyom: prepare a one‑page BOM and a draft canary plan with rollback thresholds
- Dev: schedule smoke test endpoints and an isolated test key we can run during the dry‑run

I'll convert this into a short slide and put into the HubSpot deal record.

—Marissa
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam@NimbusAnalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - proposed timeline and next steps

Sam / Sarah / procurement —

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on Marissa's initial sizing, here's a proposed plan that balances safety and procurement speed:

Planned timeline (Hosted → Dedicated cutover):
- Week 0 (Decision & Commit): Deal signed and capacity commitment (target: by 3/9) — DocuSign link below
- Week 1 (Provisioning): Redwood provisions Dedicated pool (4 nodes baseline + 2 spare) and staging test endpoints — expected 2–3 business days after commit for Redwood-managed Dedicated
- Weeks 2–5 (Dry‑run): 30‑day dry‑run with traffic mirroring at <70% production, run regression checks vs hosted p95 targets; weekly checkpoints
- Week 6 (Canary & Cutover): 2‑week canary where a % of production is routed to Dedicated, then progressive cutover. Final rollback policy: immediate fallback to Hosted API if p95 regresses >12% on any route

Technical checks & validations:
- Marissa: validate KV caching strategy and produce expected p95 delta per route
- Dev: provision isolated test key + smoke endpoints by provisioning date
- Procurement: confirm SLA and billing cadence; provide Po for reserved capacity

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-78321) and DocuSign for commitment (https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abc123-sign).

Attachments for your review: capacity-proposal-nimbus-v1.pdf, redwood-bom-gpu-estimates.xlsx

If that timeline works we can start the DocuSign flow today and aim for the 30‑day validation to complete by mid‑April.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Lee <sam@NimbusAnalytics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 19:04:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Sizing validation for Dedicated migration - proposed timeline and next steps

Aisha / team —

That timeline is acceptable. Procurement has reviewed the BOM and requested the following before issuing a PO:

1) A short one‑page canary acceptance checklist (Dev + Marissa)
2) Confirmation of SLA terms during the 30‑day dry‑run (we need a temporary SLA addendum for the validation period)
3) A DocuSign with the reserved capacity commitment and billing milestone schedule

Two quick asks from the engineering side:
- Can Redwood provide a test key and a traffic‑mirror hook so we can run our end‑to‑end smoke tests against Dedicated without affecting production?
- During the canary, we want the ability to throttle traffic to Dedicated at the routing layer (percentage routing) — please confirm that rollback is automated once thresholds are hit

If you can drop the one‑pager and the temporary SLA addendum by Tue 3/10 we'll aim to sign the DocuSign on 3/11 and start provisioning as soon as the signature clears.

Thanks — Sam
Head of Platform Engineering | Nimbus Analytics
